title: Burst cordon and soft fallthrough for rate-enforcement resilience
creator: Maya Singh
description: Context: Recent incidents showed that a single global limiter outage or skewed token lease timings can either entirely block healthy traffic or allow uncontrolled bursts that violate downstream SLOs. We need a mitigation that isolates (cordons) bursty sources, preserves fairness across tenants, and provides a predictable degraded path when the limiter fabric is partially or fully unavailable. Goals: 1) Provide a local "cordon" mode per node/region that isolates rapid local bursts without global lease stalls. 2) Implement "soft fallthrough" which gracefully relaxes enforcement to a conservative best-effort policy (bounded queueing + reduced token rate) when lease consensus is lost. 3) Maintain per-tenant proportional fairness during degraded mode and ensure SLO targets degrade predictably. 4) Add observability, runbooks, and an automated canary rollout with a kill-switch. Non-goals: this ticket does not rework the global token leasing protocol or replace durable quota store persistence; those are separate efforts.
acceptance_criteria: Cordoning: node-level cordon logic implemented — under sustained local burst (>5x baseline for 120s) node marks traffic as cordoned and applies local burst dampening without waiting for global lease reconciliation.

Soft fallthrough: when limiter RPCs to the central fabric hit timeout threshold or a configured quorum loss occurs, the local node enters soft fallthrough and enforces a conservative policy: max 30% of normal sustained rate per-tenant with a bounded in-memory queue (default 100 requests/tenant).
Fairness: per-tenant proportional sharing algorithm implemented for cordon and fallthrough modes so large tenants cannot starve small ones; unit tests cover harmonic-weight distribution scenarios.

SLO documentation: update SLOs to include defined degraded states (cordon/fallthrough) and expected latency/denial budgets. Post-degradation 95th latency must remain below 2x normal baseline for at least 90% of traces.

Observability: dashboards and alerts for cordon entry/exit, fallthrough entry/exit, queue length by tenant, token refill anomalies, and global quorum-health. Alerts for >3 nodes in fallthrough in a region for >2 minutes.
Rollout: gated deploy with feature flag default-off; canary on one region, automated rollback on error-rate regression or latency SLO breach within the canary window.
Runbook: operational runbook added with steps to: identify cordon/fallthrough, trigger manual mitigation (drain/cordon), and escalate to SRE/infra on quorum-loss events.
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight node-local admission controller that applies a short-term dampening multiplier and an in-memory per-tenant queue capped by bytes/requests.
Leverage consistent hashing to map tenants to local fairness buckets; maintain per-tenant weight metadata fetched periodically from quota service but tolerant to stale data (TTL 60s).
Fallthrough policy: fallback rate = max(1 rps, floor(0.3 * configured_sustained_rps_for_tenant)). Bounded queue with FIFO per-tenant and global backpressure if overall memory > threshold.

Circuit-breaker detection: combine RPC latency percentiles (p95 > 500ms) and RPC error-rate (>5%) within a 30s sliding window to declare degraded fabric health. Use conservative hysteresis (3x detection window) to avoid flapping.
Testing: unit tests for fairness algorithm, integration test simulating partial quorum loss, and chaos test injecting RPC timeouts and node restarts to validate graceful recovery.
Performance: microbenchmarks to verify cordon logic adds <5 microseconds to common-path request handling in non-cordoned state.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): feature branch with unit/integration tests. Local chaos harness to simulate lease timeouts.
Phase 2 (staging): enable feature flag in staging region with synthetic tenants; run load profile including 10x burst spikes and partial fabric outage simulation for 24h.
Phase 3 (canary): enable in one production region behind feature flag for low-volume tenants for 48h. Monitor degradations and automated Canary guardrails (error rate, SLOs).
Phase 4 (gradual): expand to 25% of production regions and then full roll after 72h stable telemetry.
Emergency rollback: FF-off and active drain script that stops issuing new local fallthrough queues and rejects back to global fabric (if available).
monitoring_signals: application_latency.p95 and error_rate correlated with cordon/fallthrough events
